results.title: Gender Data Ghana calls for GES policy on child abuse investigations to be scrapped
results.content: Gender Data Ghana (GDG), a think tank focused on gender equality through research and advocacy, has called for the abolition of the Ghana Education Service (GES) policy that allows it to investigate allegations of abuse internally and transfer accused staff to other communities.

results.title: UPSA urges graduates to embrace entrepreneurship amid graduate unemployment
results.content: The University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), is urging graduates to embrace entrepreneurship and job creation as Ghana’s young people continue to face competition for limited employment opportunities. The university says it is shifting from teaching students the principles of entrepreneurship to helping them turn business ideas into viable enterprises. Speaking at the second session of UPSA’s 18th Congregation, Vice-Chancellor Professor Kwaku Mensah Mawutor said the institution wanted graduates to identify opportunities, develop innovative solutions and establish businesses capable of creating jobs.

results.title: University of Gold Coast launches Gold Coast Society of Doctoral Fellows
results.content: The University of Gold Coast has launched the Gold Coast Society of Doctoral Fellows as part of efforts to strengthen research and prepare scholars to contribute to Ghana’s development. The initiative comes as the university matriculates 105 students into its inaugural PhD in Business Administration programme, with Chancellor Bishop Dr Gideon Tito-Offei urging Ghana to place greater emphasis on higher education, research and the development of national expertise. He made the call during the university’s matriculation ceremony on October 24, challenging the students to apply their education to address the country’s development needs.

results.title: NAIMOS seizes 22 Chanfang machines in Eshaem operation targeting galamsey supply networks
results.content: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has signalled a major expansion of its enforcement strategy against illegal mining, with increased attention now being directed at persons and businesses that manufacture, fabricate, transport, store, supply or otherwise facilitate access to equipment used for illegal mining.

results.title: Malawi delegation studies Ghana’s mining reforms and responsible gold governance
results.content: Malawi is looking to Ghana’s experience in gold production and mining-sector reforms for lessons to strengthen its own mineral governance, with a focus on responsible sourcing, artisanal mining and the financing of mineral-related businesses. The delegation, led by Malawi’s Minister of Mining, Thoko Tembo, met Ghana’s Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, as part of a learning mission supported by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). The engagement focused on Ghana’s mining governance framework and ongoing efforts to improve gold purchasing, traceability, production accounting and the management of mineral revenues.

results.title: JUSAG threatens indefinite strike from November 2 over unpaid salary review
results.content: The Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) has threatened an indefinite strike from Monday, November 2, 2026, if the government fails to approve its 2026 salary review and pay outstanding arrears. The association has given the government until Sunday, November 1, to meet its demands, warning that its members will withdraw their services until the issues are resolved. In a notification letter dated October 23 and signed by its General Secretary, Abdulai Yakubu, JUSAG informed the National Labour Commission (NLC) of its intention to embark on the industrial action over delays in reviewing salaries and related allowances for Judicial Service staff.

results.title: Can point-of-care testing improve early detection of chronic kidney disease in Africa?
results.content: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a growing public health concern in Africa, where early detection remains challenging due to persistent gaps in access to diagnostic services and routine screening. A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis estimated that CKD (stages 1-5) affects approximately 13.7% of adults across 19 African countries 1. Limited access to diagnostic services, the cost of laboratory investigations, and gaps in routine screening can delay the identification of kidney abnormalities, particularly among high-risk populations, including people living with hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular diseases 1–3. Evidence also indicates that risk-factor-based screening in primary care can support the early detection of CKD, reinforcing the importance of improving access to kidney health assessment in underserved settings 4.

results.title: Ghana’s road deaths demand urgent action, researchers warn
results.content: Researchers Enock Aninakwah and Isaac Aninakwah are calling for coordinated action to reduce road deaths in Ghana, citing unsafe road conditions, dangerous driving and weaknesses in enforcement. In a paper titled A Nation in Motion, A People in Mourning: A Lamentation on Ghana’s Road Carnage, the authors argue that the country needs sustained improvements in road infrastructure, vehicle safety and emergency response.

results.title: EKUMFI: How $6M EXIM participation built a $53M industrial asset — Now poised for a 24-Hour economy breakthrough
results.content: Ghana's industrialization journey may be entering a defining chapter. Ekumfi Fruits & Juices Limited is emerging as a potential model for turning development-finance investment into agricultural prosperity, youth employment, industrial expansion and export growth. With approximately US$6 million in Ghana EXIM Bank participation, Ekumfi has built an industrial enterprise with an estimated asset value of US$53 million — a modern fruit-processing facility, Ghanaian juice brands, and a foundation for international market expansion. Yet this substantial investment has lived with a contradiction.
